messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] SLO_BREACH p99(latency) > 1.5s on route=stream.resp for the last 10m. Affected pool=shared-gpu-pool-5. Estimated impacted requests: 4.2k. Paging on-call: @sara.

sara: on it. seeing p95 ~400ms -> p99 spikes to 2.1s on grafana. any obvious tenant hotness?

mike: pulling per-tenant IO metrics. tenant 'omega-corp' has sustained blkio write bursts and high queue_depth on gpu-12. KV cache eviction rate also jumped.

mike: metrics snippet:
```
host: gpu-12
blkio_write_bytes/s: 180MB/s (baseline 12MB/s)
blkio_throttle_count: 4200
kv_cache_evictions/s: 85
active_streams: 320
```

tom: yikes. sounds like noisy neighbor. are streaming stalls associated with buffer stalls or kernel writeback?

alia: i see correlated dstat: disk_io and softirq climbing around same time as p99. cgroup.io.weight for omega-corp is default 100. should we bump cgroup throttle to 50% for that tenant temporarily?

carol: we can do a live mitigation: reduce blkio weight for tenant-omega, or set io.throttle to cap writes. quick option: move tenant to isolated pool-dedicated-ephemeral if capacity available. which is faster?

sara: speed-first: cap IO for tenant-omega, then if still bad, migrate. mike run the cap command and post exact command. i'll notify support/incident lead about customer impact.

mike: running command now (on gpu-12 host, container id = abcd1234):
```
echo 'write 20971520' > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/docker/abcd1234/blkio.throttle.write_bps_device
# or use cgset: cgset -r blkio.weight=50 omega-cg
```

mike: applied write cap -> immediate drop in blkio_write_bytes/s to ~22MB/s. re-checking request tails.

alia: dashboards show p99 down to 1.0s within 45s of cap. p95 steady at 320ms. streaming stalls reduced but still some lingering stalls on gpu-12 for existing connections.

ops-bot: Deploy action: eviction policy triggered for connections older than 300s in pool shared-gpu-pool-5. Notifying connections for graceful reconnect.

carol: eviction triggered. spinning up migration pod to isolated pool-dedicated-ephemeral-2 as backup for high-priority tenants.

sara: customer impact: support reports 2 customers filed complaints in last 20m. AcmePay saw repeated streaming stalls leading to duplicated messages. severity: P2 for now. I've looped in acct-eng.

mike: logs from model server for omega-corp container during spike:
```
[2026-03-15T14:07:12Z] WARNING kv_cache: evicting prefix=acme-stream-ctx count=12
[2026-03-15T14:07:13Z] ERROR stream: write timeout to client (broken pipe) id=xyz
[2026-03-15T14:07:14Z] INFO  allocator: gpu allocation slow path, waiting on writeback
```

tom: do we have a safe rollback if cap causes higher latency for omega-corp's writes? want to ensure we don't create a different outage.

alia: cap is conservative (20MB/s). for streaming read paths, throughput is still fine. if user-facing latency climbs we can revert immediately.

sara: status update: p99 stabilized at ~950ms, p95 310ms. customer complaints down to 0 new reports in last 10m. notifications sent to affected customers with temporary mitigation note.

carol: next steps: 1) keep cap for 30m while we monitor, 2) schedule migration of tenant-omega to dedicated pool tomorrow, 3) run a forensic on why tenant IO grew unexpectedly (possible batch job or bad client behavior).

mike: filing internal ticket INF-4521 with attached flamegraphs and blkio histograms. tagging infra and tenant-onboarding.

sara: handoff: i'm leaving on-call in 5m, passing to tom. tom, watch p99 and any eviction failures.

tom: ack, i'll take it. tom -> monitoring alert channel and support updates. contact me for anything > p99 1.2s.

incident-bot: NOTE: runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/noisy-neighbor. Incident severity: mitigated (live). Postmortem required if any customer data loss or >1hr impact.

sara: quick timeline note for postmortem: 14:06 first p99 alert -> 14:08 cap applied -> 14:09 p99 improved -> 14:20 eviction+migration triggered -> 14:30 stable.

carol: adding remediation: auto-throttle rule proposal for shared pools if blkio_write/s > 100MB/s per tenant for >60s, plus alert to infra.

tom: capturing handoff: follow-up owners: mike (for telemetry and ticket), carol (for automation rule), alia (for kernel/cgroup tuning), sara (customer comms). I'll create the incident doc and link tickets.

sara: thanks team. i'll post a short customer-facing blurb for support and mark incident resolved in 30m if metrics hold. :white_check_mark:

mike: confirmed: no regressions on other pools after cap. i'll attach perf dumps to INF-4521.

ops-bot: Reminder: please run the post-incident checklist: 
- collect kernel /proc/blkio stats
- snapshot cgroup settings
- export model server logs for impacted containers
- run e2e stream test on migrated tenant

carol: noted. I'll schedule follow-up meeting tomorrow 10:00 to decide on permanent isolation or automation.

tom: handoff complete, leaving monitoring hook on.
